item.title: 3 million face masks could be used to build 1 km road, Australian study finds
item.description: Engineers at RMIT University have discovered a groundbreaking method to recycle single-use face masks by integrating them into road construction. By blending shredded masks with recycled concrete aggregate, the researchers aim to enhance road materials while tackling the problem of mask waste. Their findings suggest that approximately 3 million masks could be utilized in constructing a one-kilometre, two-lane road.

item.title: UK: 2 teenagers jailed for 10 years for arson at Indian restaurant in London
item.description: Two 17-year-old teenagers were sentenced to 10 years for an arson attack at Indian Aroma. The incident occurred on August 22, 2025, when they threatened diners with weapons. Their actions led to severe burns for multiple victims, including a couple who suffered life-threatening injuries. The court emphasized the planning and intent behind the attack, which resulted in serious harm. The motive for this violent act remains unknown.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Canton

item.title: How farmers are helping reverse farmland wildlife decline
item.description: The resurgence of corn buntings and various wildlife species showcases the power of collaborative conservation work initiated by local farmers. Through the Martin Down and Allenford Farmer Clusters, projects were implemented to improve habitats throughout their farms. This endeavor has led to impressive increases in populations of butterflies and grey partridges over the past ten years. Continued financial investment and diligent monitoring are essential to uphold these successful biodiversity initiatives.

Meet Nathan, the Texas seventh-grader who turned shellfish waste into a water-cleaning project
item.description: Nathan Gael Montelongo, a seventh-grader from La Joya, Texas, created a project using chitosan. He collected discarded shellfish shells to produce chitosan powder and tested its effectiveness on polluted water. Studies showed that chitosan improved water clarity and benefited zebrafish embryos in experiments. Nathan designed a prototype raft that could automate water quality monitoring and treatment.

item.title: Meet the Indian-origin seventh-grader who boosted atmospheric water output by 117%
item.description: Ankith Burki, a seventh-grader from BASIS Independent Silicon Valley, created an atmospheric water generator for his project. He utilized low-frequency sound waves to improve the efficiency of water collection. Testing revealed a 117 percent increase in water production under specific sound conditions. His work earned him a finalist position in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Meet the eighth-grader who built a low-cost air sampler to study rural health surveillance
item.description: Bailey Quinn Frank has created a groundbreaking air sampler designed to enhance health surveillance in rural areas. Utilizing basic materials such as fans and filters, this device collects airborne bacterial DNA. Findings revealed notable variations in bacterial composition between indoor and outdoor spaces. As a finalist in the Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge, Bailey exemplifies the use of practical tools in tackling public health issues.

item.title: Bon Jovi’s foundation helped turn former Army Medical Center into housing for 77 homeless veterans
item.description: Jon Bon Jovi’s Soul Foundation backed a housing project at the former Walter Reed Army Medical Center in Washington, DC. The development opened in 2019 with 77 permanent supportive housing units for formerly homeless veterans. The project was part of a wider redevelopment of the former 66-acre military medical centre.

item.title: 300+ objections as Maidstone residents oppose former hotel conversion into 42 studios for 65 people
item.description: More than 300 objections have been filed against plans to convert Maidstone’s former Grange Moor Hotel into 42 studio apartments for an estimated 65 people. Residents say they are concerned the development could increase pressure on parking, local infrastructure and the neighbourhood, with some describing themselves as “devastated” and saying they would not have bought their homes.

item.title: €100 typewriter turns out to be WWII Enigma machine, sold for €45,000 at auction
item.description: A German Enigma machine sold for €100 at a Romanian flea market surprised many when it fetched €45,000 at auction. The machine, thought to be a regular typewriter, was identified by a cryptography professor who recognized its historical significance. After purchasing it, the professor cleaned and repaired the machine to prepare it for auction. This Enigma machine was used during World War II for military communications.

item.title: Texas landowners feared border wall would cut off Rio Grande access; judge blocks Big Bend construction
item.description: In a significant ruling, a federal judge has temporarily halted the construction of border barriers in Texas' Big Bend area. Local landowners and environmental advocates express concerns about restricted access to the Rio Grande, claiming the barriers would disrupt the ecosystem and infringe on constitutional rights. The federal government asserts that security measures necessitate these barriers. This decision has sparked six lawsuits contesting the planned border initiatives.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Donald Trump’s climate cuts left thousands jobless; Climate Reserve created a lifeline for 50 experts
item.description: Donald Trump’s second-term climate cuts scrapped billions in research funding and left thousands of federal workers jobless. In response, climate experts launched Climate Reserve, a multimillion-dollar initiative helping displaced scientists find new roles and revive disrupted projects. The group expected to place 50 experts in new positions while preserving critical climate research and expertise.

item.title: He paid $30 for a painting that sold for $1.35 million
item.description: At a recent estate sale, a man bought a Gertrude Abercrombie painting for only $30. Upon confirming its authenticity at an exhibition, he opted to auction the piece. Titled Alderman Merriam's Shells, the painting was anticipated to sell between $150,000 and $250,000. Remarkably, it sold for a staggering $1,060,000 at Freeman's auction, setting a new high for the artist and highlighting the incredible value of art investments.

item.title: From India to Australia: How 6 countries got caught up in flydubai terror
item.description: On September 30, the flydubai Flight FZ1073 faced a cockpit attack when Omani co-pilot Hammam al-Hammami stabbed Captain Smit Machchhar. The injured pilot bravely opened the cockpit door, allowing crew and passengers to subdue the co-pilot. The flight was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where al-Hammami was apprehended by authorities. Investigations have since been undertaken by several countries into al-Hammami’s background and possible extremist ties.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Retired FBI agent’s decade-long mission to rediscover 30 ‘lost’ apple varieties
item.description: In 2012, retired FBI agent Dave Benscoter began searching for forgotten apple varieties after discovering unidentified trees in a churchgoer’s orchard. What started as curiosity became a decade-long mission. Alongside fellow apple enthusiasts, Benscoter has helped rediscover 30 once-lost varieties while preserving historic apple trees across the Pacific Northwest for future generations.

item.title: Texas city to pay $175,000 after SpaceX site it owns overpumps 128m gallons of groundwater
item.description: The McGregor City Council has reached a settlement regarding penalties related to groundwater overpumping caused by SpaceX. The city will allocate $175,000 for this resolution and commit to a 25-year groundwater monitoring program. However, residents are concerned about who will bear these costs, urging that SpaceX should take financial responsibility.
